hiddenCases.name: the vectorised string methods do the work
hiddenCases.describe: .str methods rather than apply or a loop

exercise1.hint: names.str.strip().str.lower() does both steps to the whole column, and .tolist() hands back plain strings.

exercise2.prompt: apply, and When Not To: Pass or fail, without a loop

hiddenCases.name: a score on the mark passes
an empty Series gives an empty list
no loop and no apply
hiddenCases.describe: np.where rather than apply or a comprehension

exercise2.hint: np.where(scores >= mark, "pass", "fail") makes the whole column at once. Finish with .tolist() so the result is plain Python strings rather than numpy ones.

choices: A Python loop over the values
questions.explain: Which is why it costs far more than the built-in it usually replaces.

questions.prompt: Which is the better way to add two columns?
questions.explain: Column arithmetic is vectorised; apply with axis=1 builds a Series per row and is the slowest option here.

choices: Vectorised string methods over the whole column
questions.explain: strip, lower, contains, len and the rest, applied to every value without a loop.

questions.prompt: When is apply genuinely the right tool?
choices: When the operation has no vectorised form
questions.explain: Real branching per row, an awkward parse, an external call. It is the unconsidered apply that costs.
